title: Rational Hearing — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Rational Hearing's rich face, its first round, a Sketch made in the proposal round of 2026-11: the playable handout itself laid as a band, the steward's back-row strip beside the magnifier it measured, and one made walk that ends on a blind test of the ear, the side of the line the page could only draw. I hold the fingerprint of the words each was laid against. I grow when Loudon, or a student, has taken the test and said what the ear did; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: "Lets you hear it" holds unevenly, measured on the page's own A/B wave (seven harmonics at 1/i, root C4, each dyad about 1.4 s). The thirds and the major sixth beat fast when tempered (M3 10.4, -3 14.1, M6 11.9 times a second). The fifth and fourth beat 0.89 and 1.18 times a second, so the 1.4 s dyad holds about 1.2 and 1.7 swells. For six columns (-6, M2, -7, M7, -2, T.T.) no partials meet inside seven harmonics, so tempering only shifts a roughness 15 Hz or more fast, never a slow beat. Suggested: "draws the offset to scale and lets you hear it, as beating where the two notes share a partial". The plan's A/B decision may prefer a fix in the page: a longer hold, or more harmonics.

hush-loud, found by conform and confirmed by hand in headless Chromium: the page answers rich:hush itself (line 418), so the kit leaves it alone, and its answer is setSound(false), which only sets the master gain to 0 (line 409). The context stays running with sixteen oscillators at zero gain, and an A/B already sounding plays on, because playCompare routes its dyads to the compressor directly, past the master (lines 659–661): 0.5 s after a hush its oscillators were still scheduled to stop 0.7 and 2.3 s later, so up to about 3 s of sound after the face asked for quiet, e.g. over a piece the reader just started. Suggested for the steward: on rich:hush, stop the A/B's oscillators (keep them in a list) and clear compareTimer, then suspend A.ctx once the master's fade (a 0.04 s time constant) has settled, about 200 ms; setSound(true) already resumes it. A side finding from the same code: the A/B's oscillators all start at sine phase 0, so the just dyad plays about 0.5 dB louder than the tempered one (recomputed 0.504 dB for the fifth), a small level cue the blind piece removes with random phases.

pieces.title: The miss, blind · can you hear what the page draws?
pieces.caption: **Two notes at exactly 3 : 2, walked up to a blind test of your own ear.** It opens on the still fifth. Then it pulls G a few cents off until it beats, takes the partials away to show where the beat lives, and sets five just intervals against the piano's. It ends on a blind staircase. Each trial plays two dyads, one at the whole-number ratio and one off the way the piano is off, each on its own roved note and level. Where you settle is your threshold, drawn against the piano's miss. The engine holds. Two cents off at middle C, the sound swells 0.91 times a second, as |2·f_G − 3·f_C| says. As plain sines, the loudness hardly moves (0.01 % against 10.7 %). The piano's fifth beats 0.89 times a second, so the page's 1.4-second A/B holds about one swell. Against simulated listeners the staircase's median lands within 8 % of their threshold, though a single run can stray by a third. Whether a real ear hears the miss is the test's to say, and no one has taken it yet.

verdicts.file: Rational Hearing — rich — the miss, blind.html
verdicts.why: A real test: it walks 3:2 still → beating → sines → the piano's five → a blind 2-down-1-up staircase whose answer can land on either side of the miss, and every number it shows recomputes (0.907 Hz rule, 10.75 % vs 0.015 % swing, the five ET misses and beat rates). Notes: say in step 5 that the root rove takes away the top-note step the page's own A/B gives (2–16 ¢), so the test measures hearing the ratio, not hearing the page's A/B; say in step 4 why only five intervals; 'stray by a third' is nearer 'up to 40 %'.

pieces.title: The just-against-equal strip at ×5, from the front row, the back row at 20/20, and at 20/40
pieces.caption: The steward's measure of the magnifier this paragraph names. At ×1 the fifth's and fourth's 2-cent gap is 1.4 px, hidden under the 10 px bar from any seat. At ×5 it comes to about 5 arcminutes from 8 screen-heights back, just visible. The eye needs the gap drawn five times over to see the fifth's miss; the piece above asks what the ear needs. A prediction from headless Chromium, not a walk to the back of a real room.
pieces.near: Magnify ×5 for the back of the room

verdicts.why: The section is about this page, so laying it whole is the section's substance, not decoration; it loads clean and reports its height. Its three conform errors are the steward's to fix, not this round's: two Google Fonts grants (Loudon's call), and hush-loud, which is real and is held as an offer to → rational-hearing.html.

A measurement that could have failed: it tests 'Magnify ×5 for the back of the room' and finds ×5 just enough for the fifth's 2 ¢ gap (about 5 arcmin at 8 screen-heights), and the caption matches the steward's report and says it is headless. Note: the report's own table gives 1.8 px at ×1 at 720p where its prose and this caption say 1.4 px; harmless, both hide under the 10 px bar.
